title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Because We're Going to Support You for Life! 2
content: “I see. Then it’s perfect. I have something to discuss with Kazuma-sama. May I have a moment?”
Ijuuin bowed gracefully.
It was rare for someone who disliked me to seek me out.
“Talk? If it’s quick, sure. Homeroom’s about to start.”
Glancing at the clock, it was nearly 8:30 a.m., the start time.
In two or three minutes, the chime would ring.
If it was a long talk, the timing was bad.
“Yuki-chan will be here too. Can’t this wait until after homeroom?”
I suggested, but Ijuuin shook her head immediately.
“No. I want to talk now. When the teacher arrives, I’ll explain.”
“Hmm... stubborn. Looks like she’s not going back to her seat and wants to keep talking.”
Curious, I glanced at Ichinose, who was behind Ijuuin.
She caught my eye and shook her head slightly, a troubled expression on her usually expressionless face.
(I guess even Ichinose doesn’t know.)
That added to my curiosity, but the quickest way to clear doubts was to ask the person directly.
I nodded at Ijuuin.
“Alright. If that’s the case, talk.”
“Thank you. Kurosu, come here!”
At her command, the classroom door swung open.
A large man in black appeared—the same bodyguard I’d seen before.
He had carried Gotou-kun’s desk out last time, but now he held a black attaché case in his right hand.
Moving swiftly between desks, he stopped in front of Ijuuin.
“Milady, I have brought it.”
“Thank you. Please place it on this desk. You may step back afterward.”
“Understood.”
The black-suited man bowed elaborately, placed the attaché case on my desk, and left.
The class was dumbfounded by his smooth efficiency.
Ijuuin was the first to move.
Silently, she manipulated the case’s dials, then unclipped the locks with a series of clicks.
“Ijuuin...?”
“Kazuma-sama, please look at this.”
Ignoring my question, she slowly lifted the case’s lid, almost as if showing off.
Immediately, I saw inside.
I gasped.
The open attaché case was packed full of stacks of ten-thousand-yen bills.
How much was this?
The obvious question popped into my head.
But the next moment, it was answered.
“One hundred million. This case contains one hundred million yen.”
Ijuuin’s words fell like a thunderclap, leaving me speechless.
“One hundred million...?”
Saying it aloud didn’t make it feel real. In fact, the attaché case before me seemed strangely distant.
“Yes. All of this, Kazuma-sama... I give to you.”
“One hundred million... one hundred million...”
Repeating it, the weight of the amount finally sank in.
My thoughts began to churn, calculating just how staggering that sum was.
“One hundred million yen!? Seriously!?”
“No way...”
The classroom buzzed as others grasped the meaning of Ijuuin’s words.
A wave of agitation swept through the class as people gathered around my desk.
“Hey, master! This is amazing! One hundred million! With that, you could live off the interest for a while! Nice, man!”
Hijiri slapped my shoulder excitedly, but even that felt surreal.
I felt like I was floating, disconnected from reality.
“Why would you suddenly give me such a huge amount...?”
“This is a breakup settlement.”
Still dazed, I voiced my question, and the answer came immediately.
“Breakup settlement...?”
“Kazuma-sama, please leave the Damenzu—Setsuna-sama and Arisa-sama. If you do, all this money is yours. You may use it however you like, and if necessary, more can be added.”
Breakup settlement... this one hundred million was the price to sever ties with those two?
“But please promise one thing: that you will definitely free Setsuna-sama and Arisa-sama. That you will no longer involve yourself with them unnecessarily and live separate lives. Swear that here.”
That was the condition Ijuuin laid out.
Her calm voice contrasted sharply with my fluttering heart.
“Milady, that’s...!”
“Silence, Himeno. Now, Kazuma-sama, your answer!!!”
Ijuuin stopped Ichinose and pressed me for a reply.
Her confident tone seemed to assume I would nod.
Indeed, as Hijiri said, one hundred million was a huge sum.
Most people would be dazzled.
With that, almost anything was possible, and I could live without working for a while.
But for me, that amount was just too much—too much to accept.
Thinking of one hundred million and Ijuuin, my mind raced.
Why was she suddenly offering me such a huge sum?
What was her motive? What did she want to do by separating me from my childhood friends?
I had to look beyond immediate gain and consider the future to decide what was right.
After a brief moment of thought, the answer came quickly.
Suddenly, my head cooled as if the heat had been drained.
Speaking slowly, I opened my mouth.
“...Is that all?”
“Eh?”
“I’m saying—is that all?”
The moment I said it, Ijuuin’s eyes widened.
“Wha...! To say one hundred million is ‘all’...!”
“No.”
I denied it immediately.
What she was saying was completely off the mark.
Apparently, I was being thoroughly underestimated.
Still calm, I said,
“I’m asking if, to you, the value of those two in Damenzu is only this much, Ijuuin.”
Secretly, I resolved to correct her misunderstanding.
“Value... what are you talking about all of a sudden...?”
“You said this was a breakup settlement, Ijuuin. In exchange for cutting ties with Setsuna and Arisa, you give me this one hundred million. You definitely said that.”
“Y-yes. I did say that, but...?”
Ignoring her confusion, I glanced around the classroom.
“Everyone heard that, right? You all heard what Ijuuin said?”
My classmates nodded uncertainly.
It seemed not only Ijuuin but others also didn’t quite grasp it.
Feeling a bit disappointed, the school bell rang, signaling the start of the day.
At the same time, the door swung open, and Yuki-chan appeared with a bright smile.
“Good morning, everyone! Today’s the last day before Golden Week! Finally, I’ll be free from this stomach-aching class for a while...?”
Her cheerful tone quickly shifted to confusion as no one took their seats.
“Eh? What’s with this atmosphere? Why isn’t anyone sitting? Eh? Eh?”
Yuki-chan looked bewildered, but the class ignored her, their attention fixed on us.
Hijiri, the senior, probably should have gone back to class, but it was too late to say anything.
The die was cast.
Not to meet their expectations, but to move the conversation forward, I spoke.

“Alright, back to the topic. First, about this one hundred million yen. I’d never seen so much cash at once and was overwhelmed at first, but frankly, it’s far too little. It’s practically meaningless.”
“...You’re dissatisfied with one hundred million?”
“Absolutely. Hey, Yuki-chan, do you know how much an average adult man earns in a lifetime?”
I turned to the still-confused Yuki-chan.
“Huh? You’re asking me? And is this another troublesome thing? Can’t we have a break before the holidays?”
“Just answer if you know, Yuki-chan. We’re in a hurry here.”
I urged the reluctant teacher.
She was the only adult here, so it made sense to have her explain.
“I’m not fond of people like you, Kuzuhara-kun... but I don’t hate you either.”
“Enough. Yuki-chan, go ahead.”
“Alright. Lifetime earnings, huh? If someone graduates university and gets a job, it’s about 300 million yen on average. Even private school teachers like me earn roughly the same over time.”
“I see. I looked it up too, and it’s about that.”

“But I think the hardship and income don’t match. Especially me—I was suddenly burdened with this tough class right out of college. It’s really hard! I want everyone to understand that! Please listen to me! Be nicer to your teacher!”
“Okay, back to the point. As you heard, the average lifetime income is about 300 million yen. That’s fine for a normal life, but for my goal of living off play, I’d need at least twice that.”
“Hey! That’s mean! Don’t ignore the teacher!”
I felt bad, but we students didn’t have time to indulge adult complaints.

“Now, the problem is the amount Ijuuin prepared. One hundred million yen is a lot at once, but as lifetime income, it’s only about a third. That’s not enough to live without working. Like I said, it’s far too little. They’re really lowballing.”
I paused and glared at Ijuuin, who looked embarrassed and averted her eyes.
“I’m sorry. I suppose that’s fair.”
“I’m still not satisfied. Ijuuin, you said this one hundred million was a breakup settlement with Setsuna and Arisa, right?”
“Y-yes, but...”
“That means this amount is for both of them combined. Half each would be fifty million. You’re saying they’re only worth that much to you?”
I spat out my words, and Ijuuin was stunned.
She froze for a moment, then angrily retorted.
“What are you saying!? That can’t be! Dimension Stars! are my destiny! I believe that, and that’s why I’m here!”
“Then why did you try to settle with me for one hundred million? What’s your basis for that amount? Explain that first, Ijuuin.”
I wasn’t interested in excuses. I coldly pushed away the rich blonde.
Ijuuin trembled but showing fear didn’t matter here.
Sincerity was measured in money.
“That amount... I thought it would be acceptable. For a student, it’s enough.”
“So no real basis? You just arbitrarily decided one hundred million was appropriate?”
Ijuuin nodded awkwardly.
Her pale face drained further, almost ghostly.
But I wasn’t about to stop pressing.

“Then you’re admitting what I said was right. You unconsciously judged that one hundred million was enough to separate Setsuna and Arisa from me. In other words, you judged those two to be worth less than one hundred million.”
Without letting up, I continued to accuse her.

“You thought you could buy each of them for fifty million. They’re just starting to ride a wave, so you’d get your money back in a few years. You talk about goddesses, but that’s a very pragmatic purchase for a wealthy heiress. Before being a fan, you’re a realist.”
“That’s... shopping! Don’t treat them like objects! I just—”

“Why deny it? It’s the truth. You said you want to make Damenzu the world’s top idol unit, right? The members, especially the double centers, are only worth fifty million each? What kind of exploitation do you plan? If you thought they were worth so little, why bother transferring schools?”

“Th-That’s not true! Damenzu are my goddesses of fate! I couldn’t suppress my feelings for them, so I’m here! I just want to free them from you! I can’t measure their value! Damenzu are my everything!!!”
Ijuuin repeated her denials frantically, but watching her shimmering golden hair, I snorted.
“Okay, then tell me this: when did you prepare this one hundred million? Did Ichinose know?”
“N-No, I didn’t...”
Ichinose shook her head, looking troubled.
“Right. If she knew, she’d have told me. So you must have prepared it quickly. Ijuuin, is that right?”
Ijuuin’s face was pale. She probably understood.
In a trembling voice, she said,
“I ordered Kurosu last night to prepare it...”
“Last night? So you gathered one hundred million in one night. As expected of a wealthy heiress. Impressive.”
I snorted in disbelief, and Ijuuin shuddered.
I could tell she was overwhelmed with guilt.

“Believe it or not, I’ve supported Damenzu entirely out of my own pocket. Their popularity only rose recently, so I wasn’t earning enough allowance to cover it. I spent all my saved allowance to support my childhood friends as best I could... I liked seeing them shine on stage.”
Ijuuin said nothing, only wearing a pained expression.
I looked away from her and asked Sayama.
“Hey Sayama, you said you got arena tickets for the last live, right? You worked part-time for that?”
“Y-Yeah, but...”
“And Gotou-kun too, right? You bought lots of Damenzu goods?”
“Yeah. My allowance isn’t enough, so I manage somehow, but...?”
“That’s fine. But...”
I took a breath and looked back at Ijuuin.
“Everyone’s been working part-time or doing whatever to support Damenzu for months... but you tried to buy them out with an amount you put together in one night.”
Ijuuin’s eyes widened even more.
“I’m not saying money and time are everything... but still, one night. Your ‘all’ is pretty cheap.”

“Let me ask: after being offered that one hundred million you gathered in one night, will you quit being a fan? Knowing your passion is worth so little, can you accept that? If so, I’m disappointed in you, Ijuuin. You don’t deserve to call yourself a fan.”
I doubted the pride of a single-digit fan club number.
Her eyes trembled.
I could see her support crumbling before me.

That’s precisely why I was certain this was the decisive moment.  
“Hey, Ijuuin—do you really love Damenzu?”
